messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: high queue depth on gpu-shard-22 (service: rwd-inference-runtime) — 95th queue length > 1200 for 3m. Autoscaler attempted scale->+8 but hit max_pool_capacity. Severity: P1. Pager routed to @anika (oncall) and @infra-sre

anika: digging in — seeing sustained enqueue rate spike from a customer workload, also elevated prefix_cache_miss_rate on continuous-batching path. pulling metrics now.

cory: I see the same in grafana: `queue_length{pool="gpu-shard-22"}` trending up from 200 -> 1400 in ~8m. autoscaler logs show `ScaleRejected: pool_capacity_limit` at 1767777600.

jamal: tagging pg: @ops-jen fyi in case we need to raise quota for dedicated pools. Also which rollout touched batching? We rolled cont-batching config an hour ago (canary).

anika: yes, cont-batching params rolled at 1767774000 by rollout svc: `continuous_batching.enabled=true, max_batch_latency_ms=60 -> 120`, `batch_prefetch=on`, `prefix_cache.ttl=30m -> 5m` (shortened). suspect prefix cache TTL shrink increased K/V cache churn causing more cache misses and longer per-request latency, leading to queueing.

infra-sre: confirmed prefix_cache_miss_rate spike: `prefix_cache_miss_rate: baseline 4% -> 48%`. Also `kvcache_evictions/sec` up 6x. Looks like a regression in cache config.

anika: impact summary so far: ~22% of live inflight requests are being throttled (502/slow) at 95th; observed ~18 customers with >5% error increase. Not yet customer-facing outage but higher latency and some throttles.

ops-jen: can we get a quick mitigation path: 1) revert cont-batching TTL to previous 30m or 2) temporarily disable continuous batching on shard, or 3) increase pool max_capacity to allow autoscaler to add capacity? Which is lowest risk?

cory: fastest is revert TTL and scale up pool size by +4 while we evaluate. Reverting TTL is a config flip (k8s configmap -> rollout) and should reduce miss rate within ~2min once warmed. Increasing max_capacity requires quota bump and provisioning time — might be slower.

anika: I'll do TTL rollback first. @jamal can you coordinate a quick capacity bump request with infra? If we get +4 GPUs allocated that's a safety valve.

jamal: filing short request now: https://internal-requests/reorg/INC-5242 — tagging infra-alloc team. ETA 12m.

anika: executing rollback: applying config patch ->

kubectl -n rwd apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: continuous-batching-config
data:
  prefix_cache_ttl: "30m"
EOF

Rolling restart of runtime pods (goroutine-friendly): `kubectl -n rwd rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu-shard-22`

oncall-bot: ACTION: anika scheduled a config rollback (change_id=cfg-1767778001). Notifying stakeholders.

infra-sre: logs show pod restart starting at 1767778030. warming cache — `prefix_cache.populate_ratio` rising.

cory: after restart, observed prefix_cache_miss_rate dropping to 6% in ~90s, queue length decreasing from 1400 -> 450 in ~3m. CPU/GPU utilization remains high but within acceptable range.

maria: customer impact update: tickets flagged: 18 customers with elevated latency, 3 distinct customers reported >10% error increase. ops-runbook step: send proactive customer note if rollback doesn't fully restore latency in 10m.

anika: current plan: keep TTL at 30m; keep autoscaler cap request pending; monitor for 15m. If queue not back to baseline by then, scale pool +4 if infra approves.

ops-jen: infra approved ephemeral bump of pool max to +4 (manual allocation granted) — provisioning started. keep me posted if we need to failover to dedicated CPU pools for low-priority workloads.

jamal: allocation applied at 1767778300, new capacity visible in control plane. autoscaler now able to provision additional nodes.

infra-sre: autoscaler executed scale +4 at 1767778325, effective at 1767778350. queue length immediately shows downward pressure.

anika: post-mitigation metrics (1767778350): `queue_length.p95` = 120, `prefix_cache_miss_rate` = 5.8%, `requests_throttled_rate` = 1.9% (down from 22%). Good stabilization.

cory: root-cause hypothesis: aggressive TTL reduction in canary cont-batching rollback caused high prefix cache churn and KV eviction storms which amplified per-request latencies and pushed enqueue rates above pool capacity while autoscaler hit static max_pool_capacity. Two factors: config regression + rigid scaling cap.

maria: action items — short and medium term: [A] revert TTL (done), [B] temporary pool cap increase policy for severe queue spikes (ops), [C] add canary guardrail: simulate prefix cache churn in pre-prod for cont-batching rollouts, [D] postmortem with timeline and customer impact. Assign owners?

anika: I'll take (D) postmortem and own generating timeline. jamal take (B) with infra-alloc. cory take (C) with runtime eng. ops-jen follow up on customer comms.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Severity downgraded to P2 at 1767778360 — stabilization confirmed.

anika: quick logs dump for postmortem, copying snippet of autoscaler rejection line:

2026-03-15T12:20:00Z AutoscalerController ScaleRejected pool=gpu-shard-22 reason=max_pool_capacity(8) current=8 requested=16

And prefix cache eviction sample: `kvcache.evictions{shard="22"} 1843`

cory: adding small test snippet to reproduce load pattern for canary: `python perf/playback.py --rate 1200 --model small --seed 42 --streaming off`

maria: I'm drafting the customer-facing note: short explanation, apology, mitigation steps, and offer to follow-up ops review. Will send to legal/comms review in 30m.

anika: marking incident active->resolved in internal tracker if metrics hold for next 30m. Good job team — quick detection + rollback saved us. :thumbsup:

ops-jen: reminder: let's include an automated alert linking TTL changes to cache-miss regression so future rollouts get flagged earlier.

infra-sre: saved logs and timeline to S3: s3://rwd-incident-logs/1767777777/

anika: closing thread for now, will paste postmortem link when ready.
